verdict: Edison International's revenue fell 15% and profit dropped versus an unusually strong year-ago quarter, but the utility still earned $724M for common shareholders and kept its full-year core earnings guidance.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $4.9B, vs $5.8B a year ago — the year-ago quarter was boosted by a regulatory decision applied retroactively

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Basic EPS was $1.88; vs $2.16 a year ago on both bases

kpis.label: Core EPS
kpis.note: The company's adjusted measure, vs $2.34 a year ago; core earnings were $738M

segments.name: Southern California Edison (SCE)
segments.note: The regulated electric utility that serves about 15 million people in Southern California — effectively all of the company's revenue. SCE on its own reported revenue of $4,887M; the parent company and eliminations net to -$1M, giving the consolidated $4,886M. Revenue fell mainly because costs passed straight through to customers were lower and the year-ago quarter included revenue recognized when the 2025 general rate case (GRC) decision was applied retroactively to Jan. 1, 2025.

opex.name: Operation and maintenance
opex.note: Running and maintaining the grid — crews, repairs and customer operations. Down from $1,175M a year ago.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: A non-cash charge spreading the cost of power lines, substations and other long-lived assets over their useful lives.

opex.name: Property and other taxes
opex.note: Property taxes and other non-income taxes on the utility's assets.

opex.name: Wildfire Fund expense
opex.note: SCE's contribution to California's Wildfire Fund — a shared fund that helps pay wildfire claims.

opex.name: Wildfire-related claims, net of recoveries
opex.note: Wildfire claim costs net of expected insurance and other recoveries — down sharply from $295M a year ago.

opex.name: Asset impairment and other
opex.note: Small write-downs and other items — down from $88M a year ago, when the rate case decision disallowed some past capital spending.

takeaways.title: A tough comparison, not a collapse
takeaways.text: Revenue fell to $4.9B from $5.8B and net income available to common shareholders fell to $724M from $832M. Last year's quarter was unusually strong: it included earnings recognized when the 2025 GRC final decision (the regulator's ruling on what SCE can charge) was implemented retroactively to Jan. 1, 2025. Core EPS was $1.92, vs $2.34 a year ago.

takeaways.title: Wildfire claims were quiet this quarter
takeaways.text: Wildfire-related claims, net of recoveries, were just $8M, versus $295M a year ago, plus the usual $36M Wildfire Fund expense. SCE says it has hardened — physically strengthened against fire risk — about 90% of its distribution system in high fire risk areas, and it is pushing for durable wildfire reform with a clear liability cap for shareholders.

takeaways.title: Interest is a growing drag
takeaways.text: Interest expense rose to $545M from $488M a year ago as the utility borrows to fund grid investment. Even so, the company reaffirmed 2026 core EPS guidance of $5.90 to $6.20 and its confidence in 5% to 7% core EPS growth from 2025 to 2030.

oneTimers: Non-core items cut GAAP earnings by $14M after tax in the quarter (core earnings were $738M vs $724M of GAAP net income available to common shareholders): at SCE, $18M of pre-tax net earnings from expected wildfire recoveries and reimbursements for prior-year costs (Other Wildfire Events), partly offset by $36M of Wildfire Insurance Fund amortization; at the parent, a $1M loss on the disposition of Trio.
The quarter's tax line was a $203M benefit, not an expense — one reason net income of $751M held up even though pre-tax income fell to $548M.
otherDetail: Other expense of $432M, net: $545M of interest expense, partly offset by $113M of other income.
footerNote: Net income of $751M is before $25M of SCE preference stock dividends and $2M of Edison International preferred stock dividends; $724M was available to common shareholders ($1.88 basic, $1.87 diluted). Cost of revenue here is purchased power and fuel, the direct cost of the electricity SCE delivers; all other operating expense lines are shown as operating expenses.
